entities.summary:
One World Trade Center, also known as the Freedom Tower, stands as a monumental achievement in architectural resilience and urban renewal, completed on November 3, 2014, in Lower Manhattan, New York City. Rising to a height of 1,776 feet, it symbolizes America's recovery from the devastating September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, encapsulating the spirit of resilience and hope. Designed by architect David Childs of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, the building's height is a deliberate homage to the year of American independence, reinforcing its significance in both national and global contexts.

The construction of One World Trade Center was a complex process that involved not only advanced engineering techniques but also a collaborative effort among various stakeholders, including the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, the City of New York, and numerous contractors and labor unions. This skyscraper is part of a larger redevelopment project known as the World Trade Center complex, which includes the Memorial and Museum dedicated to the victims of the 9/11 attacks. The tower houses office spaces, an observation deck, and a restaurant, all contributing to the revitalization of Lower Manhattan and the reestablishment of its commercial vibrancy.

The legacy of One World Trade Center extends beyond its physical structure; it serves as a poignant reminder of the resilience of the human spirit in the face of adversity. The building has become an iconic landmark, attracting millions of visitors each year who come to witness its architectural grandeur and reflect on the events of 9/11. The tower has also influenced urban design and skyscraper construction worldwide, inspiring cities to rethink their approach to safety, sustainability, and public spaces.
